messages:
Ariel (Marketing): Hey team — we need a fresh, reproducible bench run for the webinar next week. Can eng/runtime do a full sweep (base, q4h, q2k, int8) against the marketing payload set with latency + cost numbers and a short methodology blurb? Also need p50/p95, memory footprint, and any flaky runs noted.
Devon (eng-runtime): Yep, we can do that. Quick q: which model variant should we treat as the canonical one for slides? And do you want the exact payloads used (sensitive? obfuscated)?
Ariel (Marketing): Use the "rwd-moderate" variant as canonical. Send obfuscated payloads are fine — just keep prompt lengths and token distribution identical. We'll need a small reproducibility README so marketing folks can sanity-check later.
Sam (eng-ml): FYI KV cache warmup matters for our demo latency — include cold/warm p50/p95. Also capture batch size=1 and batch=8 for throughput numbers.
Devon (eng-runtime): Good call. We'll capture cold vs warm, batch 1/8. Can you paste the target token distribution (short/medium/long)? I'll use that to synth traffic.
Ariel (Marketing): Distribution: 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-256), 10% long (256-1024).
Devon (eng-runtime): Thanks. Plan: kick off runs on staging-dedicated-3, seed=42, repeat=3 trials per variant, capture raw logs, histograms, and perf counters. Command I'll run:
```
./run_bench --config=bench/configs/marketing-rwd.json \
  --model=rwd-moderate --variants=base,q4h,q2k,int8 \
  --seed=42 --trials=3 --batch-sizes=1,8 --out=artifacts/1912345678
```
Devon (eng-runtime): ETA ~6 hours for full sweep. We'll upload artifacts to s3://redwood-bench/marketing/1912345678/ and post a summary here.
Maria (Evangelism): For the webinar slide deck we need a 1-paragraph methodology and a single table with p50/p95 + cost per 1k tokens for each variant. Can you also call out any quality caveats (e.g., int8 hallucination risk)?
Sam (eng-ml): I'll add a quick eval: 500 sample prompts from the marketing set, compute BLEU-ish and a simple hallucination flag. Put results in a CSV.
Ariel (Marketing): Perfect. Also tag any runs that had >5% variance across trials. We want to avoid presenting flaky numbers.
Devon (eng-runtime): Will do. One more: do you want GPU config annotated (cards + mem + CUDA/driver)?
Ariel (Marketing): Yes. Full stack info please (GPU model, driver, firmware, runtime flags, quantization libs).
Devon (eng-runtime): Noted. Kicking off now. I'll post interim smoke results in ~2h.
bench-bot: Run queued on staging-dedicated-3. Job id: jb-1912345678.
(2 hours later)
Devon (eng-runtime): Interim: base + q4h done. Warm p50s look stable; int8 is still running. Quick summary attached: p50 base=120ms warm, p95 base=300ms warm, q4h p50=95ms warm. See s3 link for artifacts.
Ariel (Marketing): Amazing — can we get the raw p50/p95 numbers exported as a CSV for easy plotting? Also ping when int8 completes.
Devon (eng-runtime): CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/marketing/1912345678/summary.csv. Int8 finished, but flagged 2 runs with >6% variance (I annotated them in notes.txt).
Sam (eng-ml): I pushed the eval CSV as well: hallucination_flag,true/false,score. Int8 shows slightly higher hallucination rate — I'll write a 2-sentence caveat.
Maria (Evangelism): Great — timeline check: can marketing have finished numbers + methodology by EOD tomorrow? Need to prep slides and speaker notes.
Devon (eng-runtime): Yes, we'll finalize artifacts and a 1-page methodology README by EOD tomorrow.
Ariel (Marketing): Thank you!! Also, include the exact commands used (so audit team can re-run). If any run is borderline flaky, mark "do not present" in the summary.
Devon (eng-runtime): Will include commands, env, and a "presentation_ready": true/false flag per variant.
bench-bot: Job jb-1912345678 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/marketing/1912345678/ (summary.csv, artifacts.tar.gz, notes.txt, methodology.md).
Ariel (Marketing): Received — I'll pull the CSVs and start the slide table. If anything odd appears I'll ping here. :thumbsup:
